questions.question: What shape characterizes a normal distribution?
choices: A curve with two unequal peaks
A curve that always rises to the right

questions.question: Where are the mean and median in a normal distribution?
What is the total area under a normal probability-density curve?
What does an area under part of a normal curve represent?
choices: The slope of a regression line

questions.question: Under the empirical rule, approximately what percentage of normal values lies within one standard deviation of the mean?
Under the empirical rule, approximately what percentage lies within two standard deviations of the mean?
Under the empirical rule, approximately what percentage lies within three standard deviations of the mean?
Why is half the area of a normal curve below its mean?
choices: The curve is symmetric about the mean

questions.question: For a normal distribution with mean 50 and standard deviation 5, which interval is within one standard deviation of the mean?
What happens to a normal curve when standard deviation increases while mean stays fixed?
choices: Its center moves to the right

questions.question: Why should the empirical rule not automatically be applied to strongly skewed data?
choices: It relies on an approximately normal shape
It applies only to whole numbers

questions.question: For normal data with mean 100 and standard deviation 10, approximately 95% of values fall in which interval?
If about 68% of normal values lie within one standard deviation, approximately what percentage lies outside that interval?
Under the empirical rule, approximately what percentage of a normal distribution is above two standard deviations from the mean?
What happens to a normal curve if its mean increases and its standard deviation remains fixed?
choices: It shifts right without changing spread

questions.question: A normally distributed test has mean 70 and standard deviation 8. Using the empirical rule, approximately 68% of scores fall in which interval?
Under the empirical rule, approximately what percentage of normal values lies between the mean and one standard deviation above it?
For normal data with mean 30 and standard deviation 4, a value of 42 is how many standard deviations above the mean?
Why is a normal curve's height at one exact value not itself a probability?
choices: Probability is represented by area over an interval
Probability equals height only in the tails
The curve has no density values

questions.question: A normal model with mean 10 and standard deviation 2 is used for heights. Which finding suggests the model should be reconsidered?
choices: The sample mean is close to 10
The observed histogram is strongly right-skewed
